import: import { Sidebar, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarMenuSection, SidebarSubHeader, SidebarSubMenu } from "@zen-ds/react";

props.name: density
props.description:
Figma Patterns/Sidebar Density (6040:67524): `small` is the Basic panel with 36px rows and a Padding/Medium header
 (the rail 72, 64 for the flush themes). Unset follows the AppShell (`pattern="grid"` draws small), else medium.
 Figma's separate Side-Bar/Master/Small-Density is `variant="small-density"` (since 2026-10-21 `density="small"` alone
 no longer picks it).

props.name: collapsed
props.description:
The icon rail (Figma Expand=No). Inside an AppShell it is where the rail starts and the shell's toggle moves it
 from there, also when the Sidebar is wrapped in a component of your own; with `onCollapsedChange` the Sidebar keeps
 it (controlled).

props.name: onCollapsedChange
props.description:
Controlled collapse callback used by the Figma Basic/Small-Density header control. Without it the control is
not rendered. Ignored by `variant="workspace"`, which has no collapsed state.

props.name: brand
props.description:
Replaces the header's logo slots; the collapse control (with `onCollapsedChange`) follows it. In the collapsed rail
`logoCollapsed` takes its place; without it the rail keeps only the brand's first element (its mark), centred, and
hides the rest visually.

props.name: logo
props.description: Header logo while expanded (Figma LOGO / Union). Sized to the header height (24px; 20px in Small-Density).

props.name: logoCollapsed
props.description:
Mark shown centred in the collapsed rail instead of `logo` or a custom `brand` (Figma collapsed Logo, 28px; 20px
in Small-Density).

props.name: productName
props.description: Small product label after the logo (Figma: the product badge beside the wordmark).

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the navigation landmark. Default: the locale's “Main navigation” (“Workspace navigation” for the workspace variant).

props.name: selectedId
props.description:
Id of the current page's item: it is marked selected (aria-current="page") and its parent groups open (and stay
 open until the user collapses them), so the app passes its route id instead of setting `selected` in `sections`.
 When set, it replaces the items' own `selected` / `active` flags in the navigation (not in the workspace rail).

props.name: linkAs
props.description:
Component that renders items with an `href`, e.g. your router's link. It receives `href`, `className`, `onClick`,
 `aria-current` and the children; adapt a router link that takes `to` (`({ href, ...rest }) => <RouterLink to={href} {...rest} />`). Default `a`.

props.name: children
props.description:
Figma Body-Content (Child-Body-Content in the workspace variant), after `sections`: `<SidebarMenuItem>` rows and
 `<SidebarMenuSection>` groups, or any content. Consecutive rows form one unlabelled section. The rows share the
 Sidebar's selection, rail and `onItemClick`; other content renders as it is, so it handles the rail itself.

props.name: footer
props.description:
Figma Footer-Content (Child-Footer-Content), under a divider: `<SidebarMenuItem>` rows like the body's, or the app's
 own buttons of an Icon and a label span (the rail hides the label visually, keeps it as the name and the tooltip).

props.name: search
props.description: The slot under the header (Figma Search): usually a Search field, or a Back control over a module title.

props.name: searchCollapsed
props.description:
What the collapsed rail shows in place of `search`. Default: a Search button that expands the panel. Pass the
 slot's own control when it is not a search (a Back chevron for a module's Back + title, backlog batch 6).

props.name: overrides
props.description:
Figma instance overrides: props of the rows (by item id, a child row inside its parent) it draws, by layer (`{ "Item[inbox]/Badge-Counter": { theme: "accent" }, "Item[team]/Item[members]/Icon": { name: "icon-users-line" } }`). Written by Zen Studio;
 app code sets the sections.

props.name: background
props.description:
Default = Surface with a shadow (a Canvas/Default page; cards on the page take the same shadow, no border). Alt
 (Surface/Alt) and Flat are the only choices on a Canvas/Alt (white) page, where cards are bordered.

props.name: divider
props.description:
A Pale divider on the Sidebar's inner edge, the full height of the block: separates an Alt or Flat Sidebar from the
 page on a Canvas/Alt (white) page. Not with the default Sidebar, whose shadow already separates it.

props.name: shadow
props.description:
Figma Patterns/Sidebar/Density-Medium Shadow (6040:67524: Yes · No, default Yes). Yes: the Surface/Default Sidebar
takes Shadow/Bottom/Level-1 (a Canvas/Default page whose cards are shadowed). `shadow={false}` is Shadow=No:
Surface/Default with no shadow (◇ Master-Layout · Example A2 · Tiles, 15904:2813, beside flat tiles). Unlike
`background="flat"` (Surface/Flat, which is the page colour in dark mode), the Sidebar stays a Surface in both
modes. Alt, Flat, the small density and the workspace panel carry no shadow either way.

props.name: theme
props.description:
Figma Patterns/Sidebar Theme (6040:67524):
- `default`: a Surface panel inset Padding/XSmall from the page edge (8 · 0 · 8 · 8).
- `carved-floating`: the same inset panel in Background/Carved, never shadowed.
- `border`: flush with the page edge, no fill, corners or shadow, a 1px Border/Neutral/Pale line on its inner edge.
- `borderless`: flush like border, without the line.
- `carved`: flush, the whole column in Background/Carved.
The flush themes' rail is the panel's own 64px. Unset follows the AppShell: `pattern="grid"` draws border (and
Density=Small: 36px rows), other patterns default.

props.name: subHeader
props.description:
Figma Primitives/Sub-Header-Sidebar (16823:88101): a `<SidebarSubHeader>` at the top of Body-Content, the back
 control and the title of the level the Sidebar shows (a project inside a workspace).

props.name: workspaceAction
props.description: Figma Workspace rail: the action after the workspace avatars (usually an "Add workspace" Button/Icon-Main).

props.name: headerAction
props.description: Workspace panel header action on the right (Figma: settings Button/Icon-Flat).

props.name: subMenu
props.description: Figma Side-Bar/Sub: a 260px flyout panel opened beside the sidebar (usually a <SidebarSubMenu>).

props.name: subMenuLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the flyout panel. Default: the locale's “Sub menu”.

props.name: onSubMenuClose
props.description: Called on Escape or a pointer press outside the sidebar and its flyout, so the owner can close it.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the sidebar's root `<nav>`.

components.name: SidebarMenuItem
components.description:
Figma Primitives/Side-Bar/Menu-Item/Master (1536:27473) placed in a slot: Body-Content (`<Sidebar>` children),
 Footer-Content (`footer`), a `SidebarMenuSection` or a `SidebarSubMenu`. It reads the Sidebar's selection
 (`selectedId`), rail and `onItemClick`, exactly like a `sections` entry with the same fields.

props.name: children
props.description: Nested rows (Figma Level=Child): `<SidebarMenuItem>` children, or a `SidebarItem[]`.

props.name: overrides
props.description:
Figma instance overrides: props of the row it draws, by layer (`{ "Badge-Counter": { theme: "accent" } }`). Written by Zen Studio;
 app code sets counter / icon.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the row's root `<div>` (the item group holding the row and its nested rows).

props.name: id
props.description: Unique among the Sidebar's rows: `selectedId` and `onItemClick` name the row by it.

props.name: label
props.description: Figma Label: one or two words. The collapsed rail shows it as the row's tooltip and name.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading icon: an icon name (drawn at 20px) or a node (an Avatar in the workspace rail).

props.name: active
props.description: Same as `selected` (`selected` wins when both are set).

props.name: selected
props.description:
The current row (Figma Select=Yes, aria-current). The Sidebar's `selectedId` wins over it; a selected child opens
 its parent group.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Figma State=Disabled: not focusable, never a link.

props.name: state
props.description: Deterministic Figma State for matrices; real hover and focus apply natively. `disabled` wins.

props.name: theme
props.description:
Figma Menu-Item Theme: `neutral` (the default at every level, Figma's default; the selected row is
 Active/Neutral/Subtle) or `accent` (Active/Accent/Subtle with Accent/Strongest text).

props.name: dropdown
props.description:
Figma Dropdown: a chevron after the label, and the row toggles its group open (`aria-expanded`). Rows with
 `children` show it anyway.

props.name: indent
props.deprecated: No effect: a nested row is indented by its level (`children`).

props.name: counter
props.description:
Figma Counter (a Small Neutral Subtle BadgeCounter). The collapsed rail has no room for it: a non-zero count shows
 the Notification-Dot instead and joins the row's name ("Approvals, 3").

props.name: notificationDot
props.description: Figma Primitives/Notification-Dot on the icon.

props.name: trailingAction
props.description:
Figma Trailing-Slot (Trailing-Action on): content after the label (an icon, a shortcut). Not a control: the row
 itself is the button or link.

props.name: href
props.description:
Destination of the item: it renders as a link (`<a href>`, or the Sidebar's `linkAs` router link) and still calls
 `onItemClick`. Disabled items stay buttons.

components.name: SidebarMenuSection
components.description:
A titled group of `<SidebarMenuItem>` rows in a slot, the JSX form of a `sections` entry (Figma section label +
 Item-List). The collapsed rail hides the title and opens later groups with a divider, as for `sections`.

props.name: label
props.description: Section title: the Menu-Item section label (Body/Small), as `SidebarSection.label`.

props.name: action
props.description: Section-title action: a Button/Icon-Flat Small, as `SidebarSection.action`.

props.name: children
props.description: The section's `<SidebarMenuItem>` rows.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the section's root `<section>`.

components.name: SidebarSubHeader
components.description:
Figma Primitives/Sub-Header-Sidebar (16823:88101; ◇ Master-Layout · Example for Subheader-sidebar, 16823:89311): the
top of Body-Content while the Sidebar shows a level inside the app (a project, a space), the back control over the
level's title. Density=Medium pads Padding/2XSmall · Padding/Small · Padding/XSmall · Padding/Small with
Spacing/Gap/Medium between them; Density=Small (the Sidebar's `density`) Padding/2XSmall · Padding/XSmall and
Spacing/Gap/Small. Pass it as the Sidebar's `subHeader`; on the rail only the back control shows.

props.name: title
props.description:
Figma Sub-Header-Text: the name of the level the Sidebar shows, Heading/4 in Content/Neutral/Strongest, one line
 that truncates.

props.name: onBack
props.description: The back control (Figma Button/Icon-Main Small Tertiary, chevron left): back to the level above.

props.name: backLabel
props.description: The back control's accessible name. Default: the built-in "Back" label.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: The title's heading level. Default 2: the first heading inside the navigation.

props.name: ref
props.description: The root element.

components.name: SidebarSubMenu
components.description: Figma Side-Bar/Sub → Sub-Item: Search/Popover, then the Item-List of Master menu items (gap Small).

props.name: search
props.description: Figma Sub-Item/Search: usually <Search variant="popover" />.

props.name: sections
props.description: Grouped items with Menu-Item section titles (rendered after `items`).

props.name: children
props.description: Figma Sub-Item slot content under the item list: `<SidebarMenuItem>` rows (they share `onItemClick`) or anything else.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the flyout content's root `<div>`.

types.SidebarItem: type SidebarItem = { id: string; label: string; icon?: IconName | ReactNode; active?: boolean; selected?: boolean; disabled?: boolean; state?: SidebarItemState; theme?: SidebarItemTheme; dropdown?: boolean; indent?: boolean; counter?: ReactNode; notificationDot?: boolean; trailingAction?: ReactNode; children?: SidebarItem[]; href?: string; }
types.SidebarSection: type SidebarSection = { label?: string; action?: ReactNode; items: SidebarItem[]; }
